 Judgment

This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred against the award dated 25.07.2024 made in M.C.O.P.No.86 of 2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal / Additional Sub-Ordinate Court, Kumbakonam by the 4th respondent on the ground of receipt of notice by him.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal / Additional Sub-Ordinate Court, Kumbakonam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Despite the receipt of notice, the 2nd respondent neither appeared nor entered appearance through their Counsel.

3. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsels for the respondent nos.1, 3 and 4.
4.

The claim petition was filed by one Marudvanan of Kumbakonam, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- under Section 140, 141, 463 and 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, for the injuries sustained by him in an accident that occurred on 16.02.2018.

5. Upon consideration, the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.9,95,896/- against the 3rd respondent and 4th respondent herein (Owner / then owner of the erred vehicle).
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 27/05/2025 05:21:02 pm )
6. The learned counsel for the appellant / 4th respondent would state that no notice was received to the 4th respondent.

7. From a careful perusal of the details of the claim petition, one Maruthavanan filed a claim petition against Muthukumar / 1st respondent - owner of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.TN-31-BU-4968, insurer of the said vehicle / 2nd respondent, rider of another motorcycle TN-49-R-4439  Raji @ Arivalagan / 3rd respondent and one Pichai - owner of the said motorcycle (TN-49-R-4439).
The opening part of the judgment of the Tribunal reads that the respondents No.3 and 4 remained exparte.
8. On a careful perusal of the daily status, it reveals the fact that, on 26.03.2019, notice to the 3rd and 4th respondents afresh was ordered and the case stood posted on 18.06.2019.

On 18.06.2019,
batta for the 3rd and 4th respondents was paid or not is not known, but the adjudication is as follows, '' issue fresh notice to 1st respondent and 3rd respondent through Court and post by 21.08.2019 and the matter was adjourned to 21.08.2019.

On 21.08.2019, the adjudication made is given hereunder:
1st respondent called absent and set exparte.
The 3rd respondent is preset.
Issue fresh notice to the 3rd respondent with correct address.
Issued by 17.10.2019 and batta in 7 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 27/05/2025 05:21:02 pm ) days.
Vakalat and counter of the 2nd respondent by then..

9. After two years, on 11.03.2022, it has been adjudicated that since there was no Pichai vs Maruthavanan on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126416935/
2 representation for the 3rd respondent and 4th respondent, both were set exparte.

sentences.text: Batta was paid in respect of the 4th respondent (Pichai son of Muthu) on 13.06.2022 through Court and post.
Notice through Court was served on 06.10.2022 to the brother of the 4th respondent / Pichai, namely, Iyyappan Muthu.
Notice sent to the 4th respondent / Pichai through post was returned as no such addressee.
10. As the notice to the 4th respondent was duly served to him, it should not lie in the mouth of 4th respondent that no notice was served on him.
Therefore, the arguments put-forth by the learned counsel for the appellant/4th respondent to this effect does not hold water.

11. Based on the aforestated observations and discussions, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal stands dismissed and the fair and decreetal order passed by the Additional Sub-Ordinate Court, Kumbakonam (F.A.C) dated 25.07.2024 is confirmed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
